raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add a large-M path to the SM100 BF16x3 router GEMM. Past a shape-dependent crossover (448-1024 tokens), a Triton kernel splits the FP32 router weights into three BF16 planes once per call, and a new direct-orientation CuTeDSL tcgen05 GEMM (tokens on the MMA M side, cta_group=1/2, split-K with the existing reduce, 256-bit epilogue stores) consumes them. Below the crossover, the existing in-kernel-decomp kernel runs with tuned tile/split-K bands. Dispatch and warmup share one `_pick_config`; tuning tables come from GB300 sweeps of both tiers.

The dispatched op is faster at every measured token count on the MiniMax-M3.1 router shape (K=6144, N=128): 1.1-1.5x at 129-2048 tokens and ~1.8x at 8K+ tokens, sustaining 79% of the measured B300 BF16 tensor-core ceiling at M=16384 while performing 3x the MACs of a plain GEMM.

## Kernel microbenchmarks

Dispatched op latency, K=6144, N=128, B300:

| Tokens (M) | Baseline | PR | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 129 | 8.0 us | 6.7 us | 1.19x |
| 256 | 8.2 us | 7.3 us | 1.12x |
| 320 | 11.5 us | 7.9 us | 1.46x |
| 512 | 11.5 us | 9.4 us | 1.22x |
| 1024 | 13.8 us | 11.0 us | 1.25x |
| 2048 | 17.8 us | 13.7 us | 1.30x |
| 4096 | 27.7 us | 18.7 us | 1.48x |
| 8192 | 54.2 us | 29.8 us | 1.82x |
| 16384 | 92.7 us | 52.8 us | 1.76x |

TFLOPs vs cuBLAS baselines, same shape. BF16x3 arms include per-call weight decomposition and are counted at 3x MACs; single-GEMM arms at 1x. Ceiling = 1848 TFLOPs, the practical BF16 tensor-core rate measured on the same GPU (16384^3 cuBLAS):

| Tokens (M) | BF16x3 fused | % of ceiling | cuBLAS x3 | cuBLAS FP32 | cuBLAS BF16 single |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2048 | 709 TFLOPs | 38% | 234 TFLOPs | 26 TFLOPs | 383 TFLOPs |
| 8192 | 1331 TFLOPs | 72% | 561 TFLOPs | 36 TFLOPs | 895 TFLOPs |
| 16384 | 1462 TFLOPs | 79% | 622 TFLOPs | 38 TFLOPs | 758 TFLOPs |

## E2E serving benchmarks

Baseline = upstream `8b9a4341db`. B300, identical server flags and inputs per pair; rust frontend + rust bench driver; dspark spec-3.

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, decode DEP4 (`-dp 4 -ep`, megamoe, NVFP4 KV, 59904-token cached prefix, 1024 output tokens). All cells: range over 3 runs per arm:

| Concurrency | TPOT baseline (3 runs) | TPOT PR (3 runs) | Output tput baseline (3 runs) | Output tput PR (3 runs) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 | 8.06-8.93 ms | 8.28-8.97 ms | 2349-2416 tok/s | 2233-2481 tok/s |
| 128 | 11.35-12.11 ms | 11.36-11.82 ms | 6842-7090 tok/s | 6699-7080 tok/s |
| 512 | 21.71-22.33 ms | 21.45-21.94 ms | 14976-15817 tok/s | 15492-16083 tok/s |
| 1024 | 35.40-35.62 ms | 34.95-36.12 ms | 19803-20084 tok/s | 20181-20410 tok/s |

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, prefill PP2 (`-tp 1 -pp 2`, flashinfer_cutedsl, NVFP4 KV, 100k cached prefix + 8k input, 1 output token):

| Concurrency | TTFT p50 baseline | TTFT p50 PR |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 289 ms | 287 ms |
| 4 | 641 ms | 635 ms |
| 16 | 1823 ms | 1810 ms |

## Validation

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_bf16x3_router_gemm_cutedsl.py -v
```

**19/19 SM100 numerical cases passed on B300** (FP32 outputs vs FP64 reference, mean absolute error below `5e-6`; both dispatch tiers, one- and two-CTA large-M execution, multi-chunk accumulation, partial token-pair tail, odd-expert fallback). In an nsys trace of an M3-MXFP8 serving run, traced router GEMM time at large M drops from 14.5 ms to 6.9 ms (2.1x) with total GPU time equal between arms. dspark acceptance length is unchanged (~2.0 both arms).

Caveats: no task-level quality eval yet; all perf numbers are B300 (GB200 untested).

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark reproduction</summary>

Run each workload on the baseline and PR in separate worktrees, each with its own venv. Use identical hardware, model revisions, server flags, and benchmark inputs. The local vigil configurations are `workspace/vigil/m31f_decode_dep4_pr60376.yaml` and `workspace/vigil/m31f_prefill_pp2_pr60376.yaml`.

M3.1-Flash decode uses `-dp 4 -ep`, NVFP4 KV cache, block size 128, `deep_gemm_mega_moe`, maximum model length 131072, maximum sequences 256, GPU memory utilization 0.75, and dspark with three speculative tokens (`FLASH_ATTN`, FP8 draft KV cache, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling). A cached block-aligned prefix isolates decode:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 .venv/bin/vllm bench serve --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random --random-prefix-len 59904 --random-input-len 0 \
  --random-output-len 1024 --num-warmups 10 \
  --sweep-max-concurrency '32,128,512,1024' --sweep-num-prompts-factor 1 \
  --prompt-token-ids --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el \
  --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 --result-dir results/m31-decode --save-result
```

M3.1-Flash prefill uses TP1/PP2, NVFP4 KV cache, block size 128, `flashinfer_cutedsl`, maximum model length 131072, maximum batched tokens 32768, GPU memory utilization 0.65, and the same dspark settings:

```bash
VLLM_USE_RUST_BENCH=1 .venv/bin/vllm bench serve --backend vllm \
  --base-url http://localhost:8000 --model MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3.1-Flash \
  --dataset-name random --random-prefix-len 100000 --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 1 --num-warmups 5 --sweep-max-concurrency '1,4,16' \
  --sweep-num-prompts-factor 8 --prompt-token-ids \
  --percentile-metrics ttft,tpot,itl,e2el --metric-percentiles 50,90,99 \
  --result-dir results/m31-prefill --save-result
```

</details>

## Details

The existing swap-AB kernel repeatedly decomposes weights per token tile and places tokens on the MMA N side. The large-M path first decomposes contiguous FP32 `W [N,K]` into `[3,N,K]` BF16 terms, then uses tokens on the MMA M side with vectorized epilogue stores. One-CTA and two-CTA configurations provide different work granularities. Main-term accumulation is drained every eight K tiles, with a separate residual accumulator and a final split-K reduction.

`_pick_config` shares dispatch decisions with warmup. Ordered tables tune MiniMax-M3/M2 and Hunyuan-V3/V4 shapes; other shapes use a default table. Large-M execution requires `K % 64 == 0` and `N % 8 == 0`, with the small-M kernel handling other shapes. The large-M path requires contiguous weights. The custom-op interface and FP32 output shape remain unchanged. Weight decomposition runs on every call, avoiding persistent derived-weight state across reloads.

**Why this is not duplicate work:** this extends the existing BF16x3 kernels from [#47973](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/47973) / [#55899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55899). Open-PR searches for BF16x3, router GEMM, and references to #60376 found no competing large-M SM100 implementation. [#50177](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50177) migrates router warmup and overlaps these files; it does not implement this optimization. [#49312](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/49312) adds an opt-in external HPC backend on SM90 with cached weight decomposition. This PR improves the existing SM100 CuTeDSL path without that dependency. The open ROCm BF16x3 work targets a different backend.

**AI assistance:** Kimi Code and Claude Code assisted development, as disclosed in the existing PR. Codex assisted the review pass and description drafting. The human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line, running validation, and understanding and defending the change.
